title: In silico and in vitro insights into stigmasterol targeting Keap1/Nrf2, Bcl-2/Bax and IKKbeta/IkappaBalpha protein-protein interactions in Arsenic-induced toxicity.
authors: Soni, Manoj; Kumar, Vivek; Babu, Yangala Sudheer; Kumar, Pawan; Maruthi, Mulaka; Yadav, Pooja; Kumar, Ajit; Kumar, Vijay
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子对接和MD研究植物甾醇stigmasterol对Keap1/Nrf2等蛋白-蛋白互作的调控，对象为蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法可部分借鉴，与本课题关联度低。
abstract: Inorganic arsenic is a known neurotoxin that contributes to neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders by promoting oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and inflammation. It crosses the blood-brain barrier and accumulates in brain tissue. Arsenic-induced neurotoxicity poses a significant health challenge, driving the need for multi-targeted therapeutic agents. This study investigated the neuroprotective potential of stigmasterol, a plant-derived phytosterol, against arsenic-induced damage in mouse HT-22 hippocampal cells through integrated computational and experimental approaches. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations revealed that stigmasterol disrupts the Keap1-Nrf2 complex (E-total, - 346 kJ/mol), and may promote Nrf2 activation and antioxidant gene expression. It stabilizes the Bcl-2/Bax complex (E-total, - 540 kJ/mol), enhancing anti-apoptotic signaling, and strengthens the IKKbeta/IkappaBalpha interaction (E-total, - 687 kJ/mol), inhibiting NF-kappaB-mediated inflammation. In vitro assays confirmed that stigmasterol protected the cells in dose-dependent manner, restoring cell viability up to ~ 81%, and significantly reduced ROS levels compared to arsenic-treated cells. Neuronal morphology analysis further confirmed stigmasterol's ability to preserve neurite integrity and cellular connectivity against arsenic-induced damage. These findings highlight the multi-faceted neuroprotective mechanisms of stigmasterol in an in vitro neuronal model and suggest its potential role in mitigating arsenic-induced neuronal damage, which requires further validation through in vivo and pharmacological studies.
abstract_zh: 无机砷是一种已知的神经毒素，通过促进氧化应激、线粒体功能障碍和炎症，参与神经发育及神经退行性疾病的发生。它能穿越血脑屏障并在脑组织中蓄积。砷诱导的神经毒性构成重大健康挑战，促使需要多靶点治疗药物。本研究通过整合计算与实验方法，探讨了植物来源的植物甾醇——豆甾醇（stigmasterol）对砷诱导损伤的小鼠HT-22海马细胞的神经保护潜力。分子对接和动力学模拟显示，豆甾醇可破坏Keap1-Nrf2复合物（总能量，-346 kJ/mol），并可能促进Nrf2激活及抗氧化基因表达。它稳定Bcl-2/Bax复合物（总能量，-540 kJ/mol），增强抗凋亡信号，并加强IKKbeta/IkappaBalpha相互作用（总能量，-687 kJ/mol），抑制NF-kappaB介导的炎症。体外实验证实，豆甾醇以剂量依赖性方式保护细胞，将细胞活力恢复至约81%，并显著降低砷处理细胞中的活性氧（ROS）水平。神经元形态学分析进一步证实，豆甾醇能维持神经突完整性和细胞连接，抵御砷诱导的损伤。这些发现突显了豆甾醇在体外神经元模型中的多层面神经保护机制，并提示其在减轻砷诱导神经元损伤中的潜在作用，这需通过体内及药理学研究进一步验证。
